ledger.note: 1843: Mpande gives Natal the Buffalo-Tugela country. 'Mpande gave up to Natal all the territory between the Buffalo and Tugela rivers, which later formed Klip River county' (Natalia page; in its narrative of the settlement it follows the Natal Volksraad's acceptance of the terms on 8 August 1843, Cloete's visit to Mpande, and is not dated closer, so the event stays at the year). The region is the whole county north of the Tugela, which the republic did not hold (the Tugela 'from source to mouth' had been the recognised frontier until then), plus the Msinga circle; Cliopatria draws the county in its Natalia shape and the Msinga cells in Zululand. The zululand dossier (af-07-a) needs the matching 1843 loss.

ledger.note: 4 May 1843: Natal becomes a British colony. 'It was proclaimed a British colony on 4 May 1843' after Britain annexed the Boer Republic of Natalia (the Natalia page's infobox dates the annexation 12 May 1843); 'on 8 August 1843, the Natal volksraad unanimously agreed to the terms proposed by Lord Stanley'. The land taken over from the republic is the shape without Klip River county; the county came from Mpande later in 1843 (see the gain above).

notes: SPLIT of Cliopatria's 'Natalia Republic' row (1840-1910): the republic (1839-1843) is natalia-republic; this dossier is the British colony 1843-1910 and reviews the shapes 1848-1908 (the 1840 shape serves both: the republic to May 1843, the colony after). New slug colony-of-natal (type colony, family britain, as british-cape-colony). Five pages opened (Colony of Natal, Natalia Republic, Nieuwe Republiek, Second Boer War, Orange Free State), the budget of the combined natalia-republic/colony pair. Not settled: (1) Area: infobox 91,610 km2 (1904) against Cliopatria's 62,052 km2 (ratio 0.68); the 1903 districts add perhaps 10,000-15,000 km2 by the circles used but the pages give no districts' areas. (2) The Buffalo-Tugela gift is dated only '1843' by the Natalia page; the circle at the rivers' junction is the researcher's reading, and the zululand dossier (af-07-a) has no 1843 loss, so Cliopatria's Zululand shapes 1840-1897 still contain it (overlap to fix by the merger agent). (3) Cliopatria's Zululand shapes also contain the Vryheid land (New Republic 1884-1888, South African Republic 1888-1902), which Cliopatria's 1898-1907 Natal shapes inherit; the keyframes cut it out for 1898-1902 and the January 1903 gain restores it. (4) Anglo-Zulu War of 1879: the Colony page 'mentions the war but gives no date', so it is not recorded here (see zululand: 11 January to 4 July 1879). (5) Alfred County/Nomansland (the Griqualand East border) and Tongaland are not on the Colony page; if Natal gained them they are missing. (6) The counterpart 'transvaal-colony' (British, 1900/1902-1910; formally annexed 1 or 3 September 1900) needs a dossier; so does 'union-of-south-africa'. (7) Months: 4 May 1843 (Colony page) against 12 May 1843 (Natalia page). Gazetteer: no new names (all regions are coordinates, Vryheid, Ladysmith, Durban, Cliopatria shapes); coordinate circles for Utrecht/Wakkerstroom, Newcastle/Dundee and the Buffalo-Tugela junction could become place names Utrecht (South Africa), Wakkerstroom, Newcastle (South Africa), Dundee (South Africa), Msinga/Rorke's Drift. REPAIR 2026-10-19: the 1843 gain now covers the whole of Klip River county plus the Msinga circle (39 + 10 cells), the found event and the predecessor land carry the republic's corrected shape (Cliopatria's 1840 shape without Klip River county), as natalia-republic now does; the polygon standing for the county is to be replaced by the region 'Klip River County' when the gazetteer has it. Mpande's gift is placed after 8 August 1843 by the Natalia page's narrative, undated otherwise.
